lines: Everything under this glass is a copy of somewhere the weather is winning.
Reed beds from the drying wetlands. Coast grasses off a coast that has lost them.
We keep them warm and safe and they will never seed anywhere again.
Four thousand released this year and the register is open for anyone to add to.
A woman came in last month and wrote a sighting from forty miles off.
That is the best day I have had at this job. That is what the work is for.
I paint the unplanted bed. Not the flowers. The grey square.
Nobody buys it. I keep painting it.
It is the only honest thing in a very beautiful room.
Forty years. I have watered the Briarbell cutting since it was a stick.
It will never be the bell tree. Different soil, different weather, no bells.
You cannot move a thing somewhere safe and expect it to stay the same thing.
The pool has things in it that are not scared of you.
Miss says that is because nothing here has ever been caught.
So I have not caught any. I have just been walking through it slowly.
